title: How to Win Federal Deals Before the RFQ Drops
summary: Sources sought, RFIs, and industry days shape deals before the RFQ drops. Compete earlier.
body_text: The fastest way to win federal deals is to engage before the RFQ or RFP ever drops. Sources sought notices, RFIs, industry days, and market research requests are where agencies signal what they're planning to buy, months before a solicitation exists. OEMs, primes, and resellers who track and act on these early-stage signals build stronger pipeline and win more competitively than teams that wait for the RFQ or RFP to post. ‍ What counts as an "early-stage" GovCon signal? Before a contracting officer ever issues an RFQ or RFP, agencies generate a trail of earlier signals while they plan and validate a purchase. The main ones to track: ‍ Sources sought notices — an agency asking whether enough qualified vendors exist to justify a competitive procurement, often the earliest public signal of intent to buy. RFIs (Requests for Information) — a formal ask for technical input, capability statements, or pricing ranges to inform requirements before they're finalized. Industry days — agency-hosted events where program offices share upcoming needs directly with vendors, usually well ahead of any posted opportunity. Market research requests — informal or formal outreach where an agency is testing assumptions about technical approach, price point, or vendor landscape. ‍ Each of these happens before an RFQ or RFP exists, which is exactly why they matter. ‍ Sources sought vs. RFI vs. RFQ vs. RFP: what's the difference? These terms get used loosely, but they represent different stages of the same process: ‍ Sources sought notice — market research to gauge vendor interest and competition. Not a solicitation. No proposal required. RFI (Request for Information) — a request for technical or pricing input to shape requirements. Still not a solicitation. RFQ (Request for Quote) — a formal request for pricing on a defined requirement, typically used for simplified acquisitions or task orders under an existing contract vehicle. This is a buy signal with a defined scope. RFP (Request for Proposal) — a formal solicitation for a full technical and price proposal, typically used for larger or more complex procurements. ‍ The RFQ and RFP are where most sales teams start paying attention. But sources sought notices, RFIs, and industry days come first, and they're where the requirements, budget, and vendor shortlist often get shaped before an RFQ or RFP is even drafted. ‍ Why winning before the RFQ drops matters A sources sought notice or RFI isn't paperwork. It's an agency deciding whether there's enough competition to justify a full and open procurement, testing a new technical approach, or validating assumptions before locking in requirements. ‍ Respond thoughtfully to an RFI, or show up at an industry day with the right message, and you're helping shape what the eventual RFQ or RFP will actually ask for. Wait until the RFQ drops, and you're responding to requirements someone else may have already influenced, quite possibly the incumbent. ‍ Agencies running frequent sources sought and RFI activity in a given technical area are usually planning real, near-term spend. That pattern is one of the most reliable early indicators of upcoming RFQs and RFPs available to a capture or BD team. ‍ The coverage problem: why most teams miss these signals Most capture and BD professionals already know sources sought notices matter. The real gap is operational, not awareness: ‍ Notices are scattered across SAM.gov, individual agency portals, and industry day announcements that rarely live in one place. They're easy to miss and easy to let go stale once found, since nothing connects an early signal to a tracked opportunity or a contact. Coverage across dozens of agencies and hundreds of NAICS codes isn't a problem you solve by assigning someone to read more websites. It requires a system built to monitor and route these signals automatically. ‍ For OEM business development and long-range planning teams Early-stage signals are the raw material for forecasting. A cluster of sources sought notices in a technical area, paired with industry day attendance and market research activity, shows where agency demand is heading 12 to 24 months out, well before that demand becomes a competitor's RFQ response. ‍ The strongest BD positions don't come from reacting fastest to a new RFQ. They come from spotting the pattern of early signals months earlier, engaging the program office during market research, and having a relationship and technical narrative in place before an RFQ or RFP exists. ‍ For primes, VARs, and resellers Early-stage signals serve two audiences inside the same organization, and each needs something different: ‍ Inside sales reps need a steady, qualified stream of early opportunities tied to the right agency, NAICS code, and technical fit, without spending hours a week hunting across portals. Outside reps walking the halls at an Army, Navy, or agency-specific industry day need a current picture of what's already been flagged in market research, so a hallway conversation turns into a qualified lead instead of a business card that goes nowhere. Contract managers need the early signal connected to what happens next: the contract vehicle it will run through, the compliance requirements attached to it, and the internal owner who has to act before the RFQ or RFP window closes. ‍ When that last link is missing, promising early-stage activity surfaces in one system and dies in another, because nobody connected an RFI response to the contract vehicle or the person responsible for acting on it. ‍ How Govly helps Govly turns scattered early-stage signals into pipeline your team can actually work. ‍ Govly continuously aggregates sources sought notices, RFIs, industry day announcements, and market research requests, and surfaces them against the agencies, NAICS codes, and contract vehicles that matter to your business. Instead of a rep manually checking a dozen portals, the signal shows up where your team is already working, tagged and ready to act on. ‍ For OEM long-range planning, that means visibility into demand before it becomes a competitive RFQ. For prime and VAR sales teams, it means a live, qualified queue instead of a cold search. For outside reps, it means walking into an industry day already knowing what's been flagged. And because Govly connects that early signal through to contract management, tracking the vehicle, flagging compliance requirements, and keeping the right internal owner in the loop, nothing that starts as a promising RFI response gets lost in the handoff between capture and contracts. ‍ FAQ ‍ What is a sources sought notice? A sources sought notice is a market research tool agencies use to determine whether enough qualified vendors exist to justify a competitive procurement. It is not a solicitation and does not require a proposal. ‍ What's the difference between an RFI and an RFQ? An RFI (Request for Information) gathers technical input or rough pricing to help an agency shape requirements before a solicitation exists. An RFQ (Request for Quote) is a formal request for firm pricing against a defined requirement, typically for simplified acquisitions or task orders. ‍ How early should a vendor engage before an RFQ drops? Ideally, at the sources sought or RFI stage, months before an RFQ or RFP exists. Engaging early gives vendors a chance to influence requirements and build relationships with the program office before competition officially opens. ‍ Can Govly track RFQs in addition to sources sought notices and RFIs? Yes. Govly tracks the full range of federal buying signals, from early-stage sources sought notices and RFIs through RFQs and RFPs, and connects them to the contract vehicles and compliance requirements your team needs to act on them. ‍ Interested in seeing how Govly surfaces early-stage opportunities for your team? summary: La compañía entregó un donativo de hidratación que incluye electrolitos y litros de agua. La relación con el Cuerpo de [...]Leer más... from OXXO refrenda su compromiso con la comunidad de Sonora
body_text: La compañía entregó un donativo de hidratación que incluye electrolitos y litros de agua. La relación con el Cuerpo de Bomberos da continuidad a un vínculo construido en años anteriores. Hermosillo, Sonora, 2 de julio de 2026. OXXO y el Patronato del Cuerpo de Bomberos de Hermosillo sostuvieron una reunión en la que la compañía entregó un donativo en especie y reiteró su reconocimiento a la invaluable labor que realizan las y los bomberos en beneficio de las familias de Hermosillo. Durante el encuentro, ambas instituciones acordaron continuar la comunicación para explorar diferentes iniciativas de colaboración. Como parte de este acercamiento, OXXO realizó la entrega de un donativo de hidratación en especie que incluye electrolitos y litros de agua para contribuir a la labor que realiza este cuerpo de elementos. La relación da continuidad a un vínculo que se ha consolidado en el tiempo. Entre otras actividades, OXXO ha sumado al Cuerpo de Bomberos de Hermosillo al programa CambioXCambio, a través del cual ha realizado una donación mediante el redondeo en sus tiendas. OXXO reiteró que el incidente reportado recientemente de ninguna manera refleja los valores de la empresa. Por ello, la compañía confirmó que ya implementa acciones de sensibilización con su personal para reforzar valores como la empatía, el servicio y el respeto. ### Acerca de FEMSA FEMSA es una empresa que genera valor económico y social por medio de empresas e instituciones y busca ser el mejor empleador y vecino de las comunidades en donde tiene presencia. Participa en la industria del comercio al detalle a través de la División Proximidad Américas, de la que forma parte OXXO, una cadena de tiendas de formato pequeño, y otros formatos minoristas relacionados, y Proximidad Europa, que incluye a Valora, nuestra unidad de retail europea que opera tiendas de conveniencia y foodvenience. En el comercio al detalle, FEMSA también participa a través de la División Salud que incluye farmacias y actividades relacionadas; Y en Spin, que incluye Spin by OXXO y Spin Premia, entre otras iniciativas de servicios financieros digitales. En la industria de bebidas participa operando Coca-Cola FEMSA, el embotellador de productos Coca-Cola más grande del mundo por volumen de ventas. A través de sus Unidades de Negocio emplea a más de 392 mil colaboradores en 18 países. FEMSA es miembro del Índice Dow Jones Best-in-Class World Index y del Dow Jones Best-in-Class MILA Pacific Alliance Index, ambos de S&P Global; Índice FTSE4Good Emerging; Índice MSCI EM Latin America ESG Leaders; S&P/BMV Total México ESG, entre otros índices. Acerca de FEMSA Proximidad y Salud. La División Proximidad y Salud de FEMSA genera valor económico y social en los países donde está presente. Opera cadenas de pequeño formato en América Latina y Europa, entre ellas OXXO y Bara, además de estaciones de servicio bajo la marca OXXO GAS en México y, en Europa, tiendas de conveniencia y servicios de alimentos a través de Valora. FEMSA Salud opera destacadas cadenas de farmacias en Latinoamérica, entre ellas YZA, Farmacon y Moderna en México; Cruz Verde en Colombia y Chile; Fybeca y SanaSana en Ecuador; y Maicao en Chile, además de un laboratorio productor y mayorista de medicamentos. En total, cuenta con más de 4,000 unidades en los países donde tiene presencia. A través de sus diferentes unidades de negocio, la División Proximidad y Salud de FEMSA atiende diariamente a más de 13 millones de consumidores y genera empleo para más de 230 mil colaboradores en 13 países. Su compromiso con la inclusión, la diversidad y la sostenibilidad impulsa prácticas que buscan operar en equilibrio con el planeta, las comunidades y toda su cadena de valor.

title: Checkr and Intuit partner to streamline background checks for millions of growing businesses
summary: A new multi-year partnership brings background screening directly into Intuit QuickBooks Online Payroll and Intuit Enterprise Suite, streamlining trusted hiring for millions of small and mid-sized businesses.
body_text: A new multi-year partnership brings background screening directly into Intuit QuickBooks Online Payroll and Intuit Enterprise Suite, streamlining trusted hiring for millions of small and mid-sized businesses Checkr , the data platform powering safe and fair decisions, today announced a multi-year, preferred partnership with Intuit, the global financial technology platform that makes Intuit TurboTax , Credit Karma , QuickBooks , and Mailchimp , embedding Checkr’s background check technology directly into QuickBooks Online Payroll and Intuit Enterprise Suite , saving businesses time with a more seamless, integrated hiring process. The partnership marks a significant expansion of Checkr’s mission to modernize trusted hiring at scale, and Intuit’s commitment to deliver an integrated, all-in-one platform that provides businesses with everything they need to compete and grow. As small- and mid-sized businesses face intensifying hiring pressures, from labor shortages to increased compliance complexity, fragmented systems create delays, friction, and risk. With millions of businesses relying on Intuit’s financial technology platform, this partnership represents a significant step in building a unified hiring and onboarding tech stack for US businesses. By bringing background checks into the core payroll and HR workflow , Intuit and Checkr are helping businesses move faster, stay compliant, and compete for talent in an increasingly complex labor market. “Small- and mid-sized businesses today are expected to hire with the same speed and sophistication of large enterprises, yet many still rely on fragmented systems and limited resources,” said Kristen Faris, senior vice president of Sales Solutions at Checkr. “Our partnership with Intuit changes that. By embedding Checkr’s background check technology directly into QuickBooks Online Payroll and Intuit Enterprise Suite, we’re making it easier for millions of businesses to hire safely, confidently, and efficiently.” “Growing businesses want tools that work together seamlessly, without adding complexity to already stretched teams,” said Olivier Bartholot, vice president, segment leader, Intuit Workforce Solutions. “By embedding Checkr’s background check technology directly into QuickBooks Online Payroll and Intuit Enterprise Suite, we’re streamlining the hiring process and increasing trust among employers who are expanding their workforce.” Key benefits and integration details With this integration, scaling businesses will experience a more streamlined hiring process that includes: Seamless hiring workflow : Background checks are embedded directly into employee profiles within QuickBooks Online Payroll and Intuit Enterprise Suite for real-time status visibility. Operational efficiency : Automated, faster screening allows businesses to hire quickly and reduce manual administrative work. Trust and compliance : Checkr’s fair, accurate background check system supports safer hiring decisions and helps businesses navigate complex regulatory environments . Unified experience : Screening, payroll, and HR tools now live within a singular platform, reducing friction for resource-constrained teams. Availability Checkr’s embedded background check integration is now available to all QuickBooks Online Payroll and Intuit Enterprise Suite customers. Checkr and Intuit will continue to work together to simplify and streamline employer operations, helping businesses compete, stay compliant, and scale. To start running background checks directly within QuickBooks Online Payroll or Intuit Enterprise Suite, visit the Checkr-Intuit integration page for activation steps, pricing, setup guides, and to schedule a demo. About Checkr Checkr is a trust and safety platform that powers hiring for businesses ranging from SMBs to Fortune 500 enterprises, offering tools like background checks, identity verification and compliance screening. With a mission to create a safer, fairer world by helping organizations make trusted hiring decisions, Checkr delivers fast, accurate screening at scale. Through its suite of products, the company supports thousands of employers and millions of workers, helping to streamline hiring and protect workplace communities. About Intuit Intuit is the global financial technology platform that powers prosperity for the people and communities we serve. With approximately 100 million customers worldwide using products such as TurboTax , Credit Karma , QuickBooks , and Mailchimp , we believe that everyone should have the opportunity to prosper. We never stop working to find new, innovative ways to make that possible. Please visit us at Intuit.com and find us on social for the latest information about Intuit and our products and services.

title: Rogers and Prime Video Announce 12-Year Sublicensing Agreement for NHL Rights in Canada
summary: Prime Video becomes exclusive long-term home of regular-season Wednesday Night Hockey in Canada and select early round Stanley Cup Playoff series in English and French TORONTO, JULY 28, 2026 – Prime Video and Rogers Communications today announced a 12-year agreement for Prime Video in Canada to exclusively broadcast Wednesday night […]
body_text: Prime Video becomes exclusive long-term home of regular-season Wednesday Night Hockey in Canada and select early round Stanley Cup Playoff series in English and French TORONTO, JULY 28, 2026 – Prime Video and Rogers Communications today announced a 12-year agreement for Prime Video in Canada to exclusively broadcast Wednesday night regular-season national NHL games in English and French, beginning with the 2026-2027 season. Prime Video also acquires exclusive rights to select Stanley Cup Playoff series in Canada, comprised of two First Round playoff series and one Second Round series per year. This full lineup includes at least 26 national regular-season NHL games, beginning on Wednesday, September 30, available only on Prime Video in Canada at no additional cost to Prime members. “Our partnership with Prime Video builds on the strong foundation we have established together and reinforces NHL hockey as the most valuable sports content in Canada,” said Tony Staffieri, President and CEO, Rogers. “As Canada’s home of hockey, Rogers is committed to connecting more fans to more NHL hockey and delivering more national games with fewer blackouts on Sportsnet, Canada’s #1 sports media brand.” “We’re thrilled to expand our partnership with the NHL and Rogers in this landmark agreement, which brings even more premium live sports to Prime members in Canada,” said Jay Marine, Head of Global Sports, Prime Video. “When combined with our hit original series, blockbuster movies, and fast, free shipping on millions of items, the Prime membership is more valuable than ever for Canadian customers.” “Over the past two years, Prime Video has been a valuable addition to the NHL’s media lineup in Canada, joining Rogers in bringing marquee NHL games to Canadian fans,” said Gary Bettman, Commissioner, NHL. “We’re excited that Prime Video and Rogers are deepening their relationship through this long-term agreement, reflecting our shared commitment to serving English and French-language hockey fans across Canada with premium NHL content for years to come.” NHL on Prime will continue to deliver world-class production and innovation with an on-air team that delivers in-depth analysis and play-by-play coverage. More information about NHL on Prime , including talent and production details, will be announced at a later date. Sportsnet, Canada’s #1 sports media brand, owns exclusive English-language rights to more than 500 national NHL games per season, including Monday and Saturday nights, as well as the Stanley Cup Playoffs, with the exception of the select series sublicensed to Prime Video. Sportsnet will deliver more national games and fewer blackouts to hockey fans. Last year, Rogers and the NHL announced a 12-year agreement for the national media rights to NHL games on all platforms in Canada, from the 2026-27 through the 2037-38 seasons. About Rogers Communications Inc. Rogers is Canada’s communications, sports and entertainment company, and its shares are publicly traded on the Toronto Stock Exchange (TSX: RCI.A and RCI.B) and on the New York Stock Exchange (NYSE: RCI). For more information, please visit rogers.com or about.rogers.com/investor-relations . About Prime Video Sports Prime Video supports a growing lineup of live sports, including NBA, WNBA and the Skins Game globally, Thursday Night Football , the Masters Tournament, NASCAR, the New York Yankees, Duke Men’s Basketball and Seattle Kraken in the United States; Premier Boxing Champions in the United States, United Kingdom and Canada; the NWSL and ONE Championship in the United States and Canada; NHL on Prime and PWHL in Canada; UEFA Champions League football in Germany, Italy, the United Kingdom, and Ireland; Roland-Garros in France; Wimbledon in Germany and Austria; Premier League in Sweden, Denmark and the Netherlands; ICC Cricket in Australia; Copa do Brasil football and Campeonato Brasileiro Série A in Brazil; MLB and live boxing in Japan; and Chivas soccer in Mexico. While availability varies by marketplace, fans can also subscribe to other streaming services including FanDuel Sports Network, Eurosport, FOX Sports (Mexico), Sportsnet (Canada), Paramount+, FOX One, Peacock, Viaplay Sport, MLB.TV, NBA League Pass, NBA TV, DAZN, and Premiere FC (Brazil) through Prime Video add-on subscriptions. This is in addition to a selection of Amazon Original documentaries including Kelce , Bye Bye Barry , and Earnhardt . Media Contacts: Rogers, media@rci.rogers.com Catrina Jaricot, Prime Video, cjaricot@amazon.com Jennifer Neziol, NHL, jneziol@nhl.com

title: Pablo Larraín’s Miniseries 'My Sad Dead,' Based on Stories by Mariana Enriquez, Will Have Its World Premiere at San Sebastián Film Festival
body_text: Starring Mercedes Morán, Dolores Fonzi, Alejandra Flechner, and Carolina Álvarez, it will compete in the Official Selection. After its Festival premiere, the four-episode series will arrive on Netflix on September 24. The San Sebastián International Film Festival announced that Netflix's My Sad Dead will be part of the Official Selection competition at its 74th edition. Directed by Chilean filmmaker Pablo Larraín ( Maria, El Conde ) and based on stories by acclaimed Argentine author Mariana Enriquez, the story stars Mercedes Morán, Dolores Fonzi, Alejandra Flechner, and Carolina Álvarez. Produced by Fabula, the four-episode series will premiere on Netflix on September 24, following its screening at the Festival, where it will be presented in feature-length format. " Pleased that My Sad Dead is part of the competition in San Sebastián, an old and close festival, where our language and culture are protagonists, " said Larraín on returning to participate in the Festival. The fiction is based on the short story of the same name, My Sad Dead , by the acclaimed writer, and weaves the narrative together with passages and characters from her other works: Julie, A Sunny Place for Shady People , and When We Talked to the Dead. The adaptation was written by Mariana Enriquez, Guillermo Calderón, Anastasia Ayazi, and Pablo Larraín. Synopsis: Ema, a recently retired doctor who can see the dead, tries to process her mother's death and her own unresolved matters. The arrival of her niece Julie and the murder of three teenagers in Piedrabuena, a suburban neighborhood marked by violence, trigger a strange phenomenon that breaks the fragile balance between the living and the dead. What had been Ema's burden until then begins to spread throughout the neighborhood: the dead start to make themselves present, and no one will be able to escape the sound of their own ghosts. Director: Pablo Larraín Producers: Juan de Dios Larraín, Pablo Larraín, and Ángela Poblete Executive producers: Álvaro Cabello and Cristián Donoso Director of photography: Sergio Armstrong Production design: Rodrigo Bazaes Assistant director: Waldo Salgado Production management: Alejandro Wise Starring Mercedes Morán, Dolores Fonzi, Alejandra Flechner, and Carolina Álvarez. Rounding out the cast: Carlos Portaluppi, Germán de Silva, and Chilean actress Luz Jiménez. Download images HERE (Credits: Pablo Larraín | Netflix) About Fabula Fabula is an audiovisual production company founded in 2003 by brothers Pablo and Juan de Dios Larraín. With a presence in Chile, Mexico, the United States, and Spain, its catalog spans 44 feature films, 15 series, and more than 900 advertising pieces. Its honors include the Academy Award for A Fantastic Woman , the Silver Bear in Berlin for The Club , and the Goya Award for The Eternal Memory , as well as Academy Award nominations for No and the trilogy Jackie, Spencer, and Maria . In 2026, it will release a Netflix miniseries based on My Sad Dead .

title: 3D Printed Rapid Prototyping Is Transforming Healthcare from Surgical Planning to Patient-Specific Manufacturing
summary: Discover how 3D-printed rapid prototypes improve surgical planning, patient-specific care, and clinical outcomes by helping healthcare teams plan with confidence.
body_text: Few industries are a more natural fit for additive manufacturing (AM) than healthcare because medicine is inherently individualized, and AM is inherently built to handle that need. Every patient is different. Every anatomy presents its own geometry, its own challenges, its own constraints. Many medical devices demand complex structures, fine features, lightweight builds, or patient-specific customization that conventional manufacturing struggles to support efficiently. 3D printing changes that equation. Using medical imaging data from CT or MRI scans, healthcare teams can generate highly accurate digital models of patient anatomy and rapidly produce medical models for surgical planning, simulation, and procedural preparation. At the same time, medical device manufacturers can accelerate product development cycles by rapidly iterating prototypes, validating designs, and producing increasingly customized solutions.

title: Dentsply Sirona Advances Commercial Growth Strategy in Canada Through Expanded Medline Sinclair Relationship
summary: The expansion marks Dentsply Sirona's sixth dealer network enhancement announced in 2026, further advancing its strategy to broaden access to digital dentistry solutions through trusted distribution partners CHARLOTTE, N.C., July 28, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Dentsply Sirona, the world's largest
body_text: The expansion marks Dentsply Sirona's sixth dealer network enhancement announced in 2026, further advancing its strategy to broaden access to digital dentistry solutions through trusted distribution partners CHARLOTTE, N.C., July 28, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Dentsply Sirona, the world's largest diversified manufacturer of professional dental products and technologies, today announced an expansion of its long-standing relationship with Medline Sinclair, one of Canada's leading full-service dental distributors. Effective September 1, 2026, Medline Sinclair will begin offering Dentsply Sirona's technology portfolio across Canada, building on a successful relationship that has historically focused on consumables. The expanded relationship increases access to Dentsply Sirona's digital dentistry solutions through Medline Sinclair's nationwide network of sales, service teams, and technical specialists. Sinclair Dental was acquired by Medline Canada, Corporation in 2024 and as Medline Sinclair today, it is one of Canada’s largest manufacturers and distributors of healthcare and dental products and services from coast-to-coast. The company's strong reputation and broad geographic reach make it a valuable partner in delivering technology solutions to Canadian healthcare customers. "Expanding access to our solutions through strong distribution partnerships is an important part of our North America strategy," said Mark Bezjak, Group Vice President, Americas RCO at Dentsply Sirona. "The expansion of our relationship with Medline Sinclair represents the sixth dealer network enhancement we have announced in 2026 and reflects our continued commitment to strengthening our commercial reach across North America. Medline Sinclair's established presence and service capabilities make them an ideal partner to expand access to our technology portfolio across Canada and support practices as they modernize their workflows." “Bringing innovative solutions that enable our customers to be as productive and profitable as possible is a key driver when making a decision to add a new brand. Dentsply Sirona’s technology portfolio fits this strategy and we look forward to a mutually beneficial relationship.” said Peter Jugoon, SVP, Dental for Medline Sinclair. About Dentsply Sirona Dentsply Sirona is the world’s largest diversified manufacturer of professional dental products and technologies, with over a century of innovation and service to the dental industry and patients worldwide. Dentsply Sirona develops, manufactures, and markets a comprehensive solutions offering including dental and oral health products as well as other consumable medical devices under a strong portfolio of world-class brands. Dentsply Sirona’s innovative products provide high-quality, effective and connected solutions to advance patient care and deliver better and safer dental care. Dentsply Sirona is headquartered in Charlotte, North Carolina. The Company’s shares are listed in the United States on Nasdaq under the symbol XRAY. title: How Agencies With Ecommerce Clients Can Use an Ad Management Platform to Bring Results
summary: How Agencies With Ecommerce Clients Can Use an Ad Management Platform to Bring Results by Logan Welbaum
body_text: Running paid ads for ecommerce clients is one of the most demanding parts of agency work. You are managing multiple stores, multiple product lines, and multiple ad accounts, all at the same time. Budgets shift, creatives go stale fast, and every client wants to see results before the month is out. The pressure is real, and the margin for error is thin. This is where an ad management platform built specifically for ecommerce makes a genuine difference. Not just as a tool to save time, but as a system that helps agencies produce better outcomes for the clients who trust them most. Why Agencies a Dedicated Ad Management Platform For Ecommerce Clients Ecommerce advertising is not the same as running ads for a service business or a local brand. A product-based store has a completely different rhythm. New SKUs get added regularly. Seasonal spikes need to be anticipated. Winning products need to be scaled fast before the window closes, and underperformers need to be cut before they drain the budget. Manual Management is not sustainable. Managing all of this manually, with separate logins for Meta, Google, and TikTok, spreadsheets for tracking, and a constant back-and-forth between tools, is not sustainable at any real scale. Agencies that try to run ecommerce clients this way end up spending more time on administration than on actual strategy. The client suffers for it. Everything comes into one place. A purpose-built ad management platform brings everything into one place. Campaign creation, creative production, performance tracking, and optimization all happen under one roof. That is not just a convenience; it is a structural advantage. It means your team can take on more clients without sacrificing quality, and it means your clients get faster decisions, fresher creatives, and tighter feedback loops on what is working. The global AI for ecommerce market is on a significant growth trajectory. Agencies that build their workflows around smart, integrated platforms are now positioning themselves to handle that growth rather than scramble to catch up with it. How the Best Ad Management Platform Helps Agency Clients The difference between a generic marketing tool and one built for ecommerce is felt immediately in practice. Platforms like Plai are designed around the actual workflow of product-based advertising, from creative generation through to campaign launch and daily optimization. Here is how the right platform directly benefits the ecommerce clients your agency serves. Faster Creative Production Without Compromising Quality For ecommerce brands, creative is the engine of performance. A product image sitting in an ad set without strong visual treatment and sharp copy will not convert, no matter how well the targeting is built. The challenge is that producing great creatives at volume, across different formats, platforms, and product lines, takes time that most agencies do not have in abundance. Plai's AI Creative Studio addresses this directly. It takes product images and transforms them into scroll-stopping ad formats, including video, UGC-style content, and memes built for social feeds. The output is not generic; it is built around the brand's own visual identity. For agencies managing multiple ecommerce clients, this means each brand maintains its own distinct look and feel without requiring a separate design workflow for every single asset. Creatives that used to take days can be produced in minutes. Launching Campaigns Across Channels Without the Usual Friction One of the biggest time sinks in ecommerce ad management is the actual process of launching. Setting up campaigns individually across Meta, Google, and TikTok, each with their own interfaces, requirements, and quirks, creates unnecessary drag. By the time a campaign goes live, the opportunity window may have already shifted. Plai consolidates this into a single launch workflow. You can push campaigns across Meta, Google, TikTok, and more from one platform, with AI-generated copy and targeting built in. title: Cold Calling Skills for B2B Sales: 14 Expert Tactics to Increase Your Close Rate
summary: Cold calling skills for B2B sales require expertise in conversational skills, research and plenty of other tactics. Here's how you can increase your closing rate with these insights. Read on...
body_text: Quick Answer: Successful B2B cold calling requires mastering both soft skills; relatability, critical thinking, resilience, and positive tone; and hard skills like research, strategic timing, and objection handling. While the average success rate is 2.3%, top performers achieve 6.7-15% by combining quality data with refined technique. Cold calling remains one of the most powerful B2B channels, contributing over 50% of leads for growing companies when executed with skill and persistence. If you've been in B2B sales for more than a minute, you've probably heard the familiar refrain: "Cold calling is dead." It's a comforting thought when you're staring at a list of numbers, but the data tells a completely different story. Cold calling remains one of the most powerful tools in your arsenal, provided you have the right strategy. In fact, recent industry analysis reveals that cold calling contributes over 50% of B2B leads for growing companies. That's a massive slice of the pipeline you simply can't afford to ignore. The real problem isn't the medium itself; it's how most reps approach it. We expect instant gratification, but successful B2B outreach requires serious persistence. Studies show that a staggering 93% of successful conversions happen after six or more follow-ups. Yet, the majority of reps throw in the towel after just one or two attempts. If you want to stop leaving money on the table, it's time to refine your approach. Here are seven expert tactics to elevate your cold calling skills and significantly boost your close rate. Does Cold Calling Still Work in B2B Sales in 2026? Latest Cold Calling Stats Absolutely. Cold calling remains one of the most effective channels for B2B sales teams, but only when you combine it with the right cold calling skills and strategic execution. Key Statistics: 50%+ of B2B leads originate from cold calling , making it impossible to ignore as a revenue driver for growth-focused companies. 82% of buyers are open to meetings from cold calls , proving that decision-makers haven't abandoned the phone as a communication channel. High-performing teams achieve 6.7% to 15% success rates by leveraging quality data, precise timing, and refined cold calling skills. The reality is that cold calling has evolved. It's no longer about volume dialing and generic pitches. Today's successful reps understand that cold calling skills — like strategic timing, personalization, and persistence — are what separate quota-crushers from struggling performers. The average success rate of 2.3% exists because most reps lack these critical skills. They call at the wrong times, they haven't researched their prospects, and they give up after one or two rejections. But when you master the fundamentals and apply data-driven tactics, you can triple or even quadruple your success rate. The channel isn't dead. Your approach to it might be. While mastering cold calling skills is essential, the right technology amplifies your efforts. AI power dialers combine intelligent dialing acceleration with real-time coaching to help you execute these skills at scale without sacrificing the quality of each conversation How to Master Cold Calling Skills: 7 Expert Tactics for B2B Sales The gap between a sales rep who hits quota and one who struggles often comes down to one thing: a mastery of fundamental cold calling skills. It's not about having the perfect script or the loudest voice; it's about executing a complex set of behaviors that build trust and drive action in a matter of seconds. When we talk about expert tactics for B2B sales, we're really talking about a hybrid skill set. You need the technical proficiency to navigate complex organizational structures and the emotional intelligence to connect with a stranger instantly. The modern buyer is sophisticated. They can spot a generic pitch from a mile away. To break through the noise, you need a balanced approach. This means developing both the intangible human elements that make conversations flow and the rigid, process-driven techniques that keep your pipeline full. In this section, we'll break down the essential cold calling skills into two distinct categories: soft skills and hard skills. By mastering both sides of this equation, you transform cold calling from a dreaded task into a predictable revenue engine. Let's dive into the core competencies every top performer relies on. What Are the Essential Soft Skills for Cold Calling Success? Essential Skills For Cold Calls Soft skills are the invisible engine behind every successful cold call. They are the interpersonal attributes and emotional intelligence traits that allow you to connect with prospects on a human level. While hard skills get you to the right person, soft skills are what keep them on the line. These skills dictate how you handle rejection, how you adapt to unexpected responses, and how you make a stranger feel understood in less than thirty seconds. Without a strong foundation in these areas, even the most meticulously researched pitch will fall flat. They are often harder to teach than technical processes because they require self-awareness and emotional regulation. However, mastering these intangible traits — like your ability to bounce back from a harsh "no" or your capacity to sound genuinely helpful rather than pushy — is the ultimate differentiator in B2B sales. How to Build Relatability in Sales: Connecting with Prospects Instantly Relatability is the art of closing the psychological distance between you and the prospect. It's the skill that transforms you from a "bothersome salesperson" into a "trusted peer." When a prospect answers the phone, their guard is up. Your immediate goal isn't to pitch; it's to disarm. This requires matching their tone, pacing, and energy — a technique often called mirroring. If they are speaking quickly and formally, you match that efficiency. If they are more relaxed, you soften your approach. Consider a scenario where you're calling a busy Chief Marketing Officer. Instead of launching into a high-energy monologue, you might say, "I know you're likely in the middle of a campaign sprint, so I'll be brief." This shows empathy for their specific world. The data supports this human-centric approach: using inclusive language like "we" and "our" instead of "I" and "you" can increase meeting booking rates by up to 55%. Example in Action: Instead of: "I want to show you how my product helps your team." Try: "We've been seeing a lot of marketing leaders struggle with attribution this quarter. Is that something your team is currently navigating?" This subtle shift in language makes the conversation collaborative rather than adversarial, establishing a relatable foundation for the rest of the call. Your opening line is critical—it's your chance to disarm the prospect and establish relatability. Learn specific cold call openers that demonstrate empathy for their world and show you've done your research, transforming a generic pitch into a collaborative conversation Why Critical Thinking is the Most Underrated Sales Skill Critical thinking in cold calling is your ability to process new information in real-time and pivot your strategy instantly. It's the opposite of reading blindly from a script. When a prospect throws a curveball — a unique objection, a competitor mention, or a specific pain point you didn't anticipate — your critical thinking skills dictate whether the call lives or dies. You must rapidly analyze what they said, understand the underlying implication, and formulate a relevant, value-driven response. This skill is crucial because no two calls are identical. A rigid approach will fail when confronted with complex B2B buying scenarios. Interestingly, top-performing reps ask an average of 11 to 14 targeted questions during a successful cold call. You can't ask insightful, probing questions if you aren't critically analyzing the prospect's previous answers. Example in Action: A prospect says, "We already use Software X, and it's fine." A rep lacking critical thinking might just say, "Okay, thanks," and hang up. A critical thinker analyzes the word "fine." Response: "I hear that a lot. Software X is great for basic reporting. When you say it's 'fine,' are you finding it handles your multi-touch attribution, or are you still pulling those reports manually?" This pivots the conversation from a dead-end to a targeted discovery of a potential gap in their current solution. How to Build Resilience and Handle Rejection in Sales Art of Resilience In Cold Calls Resilience is the psychological armor every cold caller must wear. It is the capacity to absorb rejection, hostility, and indifference without letting it impact your performance on the very next dial. In B2B sales, rejection is not an anomaly; it is the statistical norm. The reality is that the average cold calling success rate hovers around a mere 2.3% . This means you will hear "no" vastly more often than you hear "yes." Without resilience, reps experience call reluctance, burnout, and a sharp decline in tone quality. A resilient rep understands that a rejection is not a personal indictment; it's simply a data point indicating bad timing or a poor fit. They maintain emotional equilibrium. Example in Action: You make a call, and the prospect aggressively says, "Take me off your list, I don't have time for this!" and hangs up. A non-resilient rep might need a ten-minute break, letting their anxiety spike before the next call. A resilient rep logs the outcome in the CRM, takes a single deep breath, and dials the next number with the exact same upbeat, professional tone they used on the first call of the day. They separate the outcome of the previous call from the potential of the next one. Resilience and positive tone are critical soft skills, but they're even more powerful when paired with real-time call coaching that surfaces objection-handling guidance and battlecards during live conversations, helping you maintain confidence and composure through high-volume calling sessions. Maintaining Positivity in Sales: Why Tone Matters More Than Words How To Stay Calm and Positive In Cold Calls Positivity in cold calling isn't about being overly enthusiastic or artificially cheerful; it's about projecting confidence, warmth, and a genuine belief in the value you offer. Your tone of voice transmits your attitude before you even finish your first sentence. Prospects can hear a smile, and conversely, they can hear defeat, boredom, or desperation. If you sound like you expect to be rejected, the prospect will happily oblige. This auditory positivity is a critical component of your cold calling skills. Research indicates that starting a call with a positive, friendly opener — such as a warm "How have you been?" — can increase success rates by 6.6x compared to standard, rigid corporate greetings. Example in Action: It's 4:30 PM on a Friday. You've made 60 dials and haven't booked a single meeting. Negative Tone: (Sighs) "Hi, this is John from TechCorp... do you have a minute?" (Sounds exhausted and apologetic). Positive Tone: "Hi Sarah! It's John from TechCorp. I know it's late on a Friday, but I was hoping to catch you before the weekend..." (Sounds energetic, empathetic, and confident). Even at the end of a grueling day, maintaining that baseline of professional positivity makes the prospect feel like they are speaking to a peer who is excited to help them, rather than a beaten-down telemarketer. What Are the Core Hard Skills for B2B Cold Calling? Main Components of a Stable Cold Calling Engine While soft skills govern how you interact, hard skills dictate what you actually do. These are the measurable, process-oriented, and highly trainable techniques that form the mechanics of a cold call. Hard skills encompass the entire lifecycle of the outreach process, from the pre-call preparation to the final attempt to secure a meeting on the calendar. These competencies rely heavily on methodology, data utilization, and product expertise. If you lack hard skills, you might have a very pleasant conversation with a prospect, but you will fail to uncover their business pain, navigate their objections, or drive the interaction toward a measurable sales outcome. Mastering these technical elements is what turns a friendly chat into a qualified pipeline opportunity. B2B Sales Research: How to Prepare for a Cold Call Here's Why Conducting Thorough Research Is Important Research is the foundation of any effective cold outreach strategy. It is the hard skill of gathering, analyzing, and synthesizing data about a prospect and their company before you ever pick up the phone. In the modern B2B landscape, generic "spray and pray" tactics are dead. You must understand the prospect's industry, their company's recent news, and their specific role within the organization. Failing to research is a surefire way to lose credibility instantly. In fact, 82% of decision-makers report that sales reps often come across as unprepared during calls. Effective research allows you to craft a hypothesis about the prospect's pain points, making your outreach highly relevant. Example in Action: Instead of calling a VP of HR blindly, you spend three minutes researching. You notice on LinkedIn that they just acquired a smaller company, and on their careers page, they are hiring aggressively. Your opening: "Hi Mark, I saw the recent news about the acquisition of Company Y — congratulations. Usually, when teams scale that quickly, onboarding and payroll integration become a massive headache. Is your team currently managing that transition manually?" This demonstrates immediate value and proves you aren't just reading from a list. Mastering these cold calling skills is foundational, but pairing them with the right software multiplies your impact. The best cold calling software tools combine dialing efficiency, real-time coaching, and CRM integration to help you execute these tactics consistently across your entire team Effective Prospecting Skills: Building a High-Quality Call List How To Maintain Focus During Cold Calling Prospecting is the systematic hard skill of identifying and qualifying potential buyers who fit your Ideal Customer Profile (ICP). It's not just about finding names and numbers; it's about finding the right names and the right numbers. Poor prospecting leads to wasted dials, low morale, and terrible conversion rates. This skill involves using databases, LinkedIn Sales Navigator, and intent data to build targeted lists. The quality of your prospecting directly impacts your connection rates. Data shows that when sales teams use verified, high-quality contact databases, their answer rates can jump to 13.3% — which is remarkably close to the connection rates of warm leads. Example in Action: A rep with poor prospecting skills downloads a generic list of "Marketing Managers in the US" and starts dialing, hitting mostly gatekeepers or disconnected numbers. A rep with strong prospecting skills filters their search: "Director of Demand Generation," at SaaS companies with 50–200 employees, who use HubSpot, and have recently posted about lead quality. They then use a data enrichment tool to find verified direct-dial mobile numbers. They make fewer calls, but have significantly more high-quality conversations. Value Delivery in Sales: Crafting a Compelling Pitch Value Delivery Tactics During Cold Calls Value delivery is the hard skill of articulating exactly how your product or service solves a specific, painful problem for the prospect — and doing it concisely. It is the translation of complex product features into clear, bottom-line business benefits. On a cold call, you don't have time for a full presentation; you have seconds to deliver a "hook" that earns you the right to continue the conversation. This skill requires a deep understanding of your buyer personas and the metrics they care about (e.g., time saved, revenue generated, risk mitigated). Being upfront and clear about this value is critical; stating your reason for calling clearly can boost success rates by 2.1x. Example in Action: Feature-dumping (Poor Value Delivery): "We sell a cloud-based CRM with AI routing, predictive analytics, and custom dashboarding." Value Delivery (Strong): "We help VPs of Sales like you reduce the time reps spend on admin work by about 30%, giving them back two hours a day to actually sell. If I could show you how we did that for [Competitor Name], would you be open to a brief conversation next week?" The second approach focuses entirely on the outcome — time saved, more selling — rather than the technical features. The Art of Questioning: Uncovering Pain Points on a Cold Call Mastering The Art of Subtle Questioning Questioning is perhaps the most strategic hard skill in a cold caller's toolkit. It is the method by which you uncover pain, qualify the prospect, and guide them toward recognizing their own need for your solution. Effective questioning moves the prospect off their defensive script and gets them talking about their business. This isn't about interrogating the prospect; it's about asking open-ended, thought-provoking questions that challenge their status quo. Top-performing calls typically involve the rep asking 11 to 14 questions. The quality of your questions dictates the quality of the information you receive. Example in Action: Closed Question (Poor): "Are you happy with your current IT provider?" (Answer: "Yes." Call over.) Open-Ended Question (Strong): "When you look at your IT infrastructure right now, what's the one bottleneck that's slowing down your remote team the most?" This forces the prospect to think critically about their operations and provides you with a specific pain point to anchor your value proposition against. Gatekeeper Navigation: Strategies for Reaching the Decision Maker How to Handle Gatekeepers Like a Pro Gatekeeper navigation is the tactical skill of working with — not against — executive assistants, receptionists, and office managers to reach your target prospect. Gatekeepers are trained to block unsolicited sales calls. If you treat them as obstacles, you will fail. If you treat them as valuable resources and allies, they can be your greatest asset. This skill involves projecting executive presence, using assumed familiarity, and asking the right questions to gather intelligence even if you don't get patched through. A staggering 71% of reps say that getting past gatekeepers is their biggest hurdle in cold calling. Example in Action: Adversarial approach: "Put me through to the CEO." (Gatekeeper: "He's not available, send an email.") Collaborative approach: "Hi there, I was hoping you could help me out. I need to speak with whoever handles your cybersecurity compliance, and I want to make sure I'm not bothering the wrong person. Would that be Sarah in IT, or does someone else manage that?" By asking for help and demonstrating that you value their time and knowledge, the gatekeeper is much more likely to point you in the right direction or put you through. Objection Handling Techniques: Turning a 'No' into a 'Maybe' How To Increase Acceptance Rate In Sales Calls? Objection handling is the hard skill of anticipating , isolating, and resolving the reasons a prospect gives for not wanting to meet or buy. Objections on a cold call are rarely final; they are usually reflex responses designed to get you off the phone (e.g., "We don't have budget," "Send me an email," "Call me in six months"). Mastering this skill means not taking the first "no" at face value. It requires a framework — like the classic Listen, Acknowledge, Explore, Respond (LAER) model — to dig deeper into the real concern. Example in Action: Prospect: "Just send me an email with some info." Poor handling: "Okay, what's your email address?" (You will never hear from them again). Strong handling: "I can absolutely do that. Just so I don't send you a generic 20-page PDF that wastes your time, what is your primary focus right now: reducing churn or increasing acquisition?" This acknowledges their request but uses a strategic question to keep them engaged and uncover actual pain, transforming a brush-off into a real conversation. Competitor and Product Knowledge: Win the Comparison Every Time Product and competitor knowledge is the foundational hard skill of knowing exactly what you sell, how it works, and how it compares to every other option in the market. If you hesitate, guess, or provide incorrect information when a prospect asks a technical question or brings up a competitor, your credibility evaporates instantly. You don't need to be an engineer, but you must understand your competitive differentiators — your "moat." Prospects are highly educated; 96% of them do their own research before engaging with sales. You must know more about the market landscape than they do. Example in Action: Prospect: "We're currently looking at [Major Competitor]. Why should we talk to you?" Poor response: "Well, our product is better and we have great customer service." Strong response: "[Major Competitor] makes a great product, especially for enterprise-level reporting. However, where we typically win against them is in implementation speed. They usually take 6 months to deploy; we have teams fully onboarded in 30 days. Is speed to value a priority for this project?" This shows deep market knowledge, respects the competitor, and highlights a specific, measurable advantage. Sales Note-Taking Skills: Maximizing CRM Data Retain and Maximize Your Note Taking Skills Note-taking is the administrative hard skill of accurately and efficiently recording the intelligence gathered during a cold call into your CRM. While it may seem mundane, it is critical for long-term success. A cold call is a data-gathering exercise. If you don't document the prospect's tech stack, pain points, or timeline, that data is lost forever. Effective note-taking ensures that when you follow up — which, as data shows, you must do multiple times — you can reference specific details from the previous conversation, proving you listened and building trust. Reps spend up to 35% of their time on administrative tasks; efficient note-taking skills streamline this process. Example in Action: Poor notes: "Called John. Not interested right now. Call back Q3." Strong notes: "Connected with John (VP Ops). Currently using legacy on-prem system. Main pain point: server maintenance costs are 20% over budget. No budget until October. Action: Set task to follow up Sept 15th with case study on cloud migration cost savings." The second set of notes provides a highly specific, actionable blueprint for the next touchpoint. How to Close on a Cold Call: Securing the Next Step Prioritize Meetings Over Potentially Difficult Sales Calls Closing on a cold call does not mean selling the product; it means successfully securing the next logical step in the sales process — which is almost always a booked meeting or discovery call. It is the hard skill of asking for a micro-commitment with confidence and clarity. Many reps do the hard work of building rapport and delivering value, but then fail to ask for the meeting definitively. You must make it easy for the prospect to say yes by proposing a specific time or offering a clear alternative. Example in Action: Weak close: "So, do you think you'd want to learn more sometime?" Strong close: "Based on what you mentioned about your lead routing issues, I think it makes sense for us to set up a 15-minute call where I can show you exactly how we fixed that for [Similar Company]. Do you have your calendar handy? How does next Tuesday at 10 AM look for you?" This close is presumptive, specific, and tied directly to the value uncovered during the call. Building Rapport in B2B Sales: The Bridge Between Hard and Soft Skills Mastering Rapport and Bonding During Sales Campaigns Building rapport is a unique competency that bridges the gap between soft and hard skills. It utilizes the emotional intelligence of relatability (soft) but relies on the tactical execution of research and questioning (hard) to create a genuine business connection. Rapport in B2B sales isn't about talking about the weather or sports; it's about establishing professional credibility and mutual respect. It is the skill of making the prospect feel that you are an expert who understands their industry and their specific challenges. While Friday afternoons are notoriously bad for booking meetings, data shows they are actually the most productive days for building these types of relationships and rapport with prospects. Example in Action: Instead of forced small talk ("How's the weather in Chicago?"), a skilled rep builds business rapport based on industry knowledge. "I noticed your team just expanded into the EMEA market. I was speaking with another logistics VP last week who said dealing with the new customs regulations has been a nightmare. Has your team hit those same roadblocks yet?" This builds immediate rapport because it proves you speak their language, understand their world, and are engaging with them as a peer facing similar industry challenges. Tips for Sharpening Your Cold Calling Skills: How Top B2B Reps Stay Ahead Great cold calling skills are never static. The best reps in B2B sales treat their craft like a professional athlete treats their sport — always training, always refining, always looking for a competitive edge. Whether you're a seasoned SDR or a newly promoted AE, there are clear, actionable habits that separate those who plateau from those who consistently improve. From structured coaching to staying ahead of industry shifts, the following strategies will help you build a continuous improvement mindset that keeps your cold calling performance sharp, relevant, and consistently above the industry average. How Sales Coaching and Call Feedback Loops Accelerate Cold Calling Improvement One of the fastest ways to improve your cold calling skills is to put your calls under a microscope. Recording and reviewing your calls — ideally with a manager or peer — reveals patterns you simply cannot detect in the moment. Are you talking too much? Are you asking closed questions? Are you stumbling on the same objection repeatedly? Structured feedback sessions transform these blind spots into deliberate practice targets. Reps who receive consistent, specific coaching improve their close rates significantly faster than those who rely on experience alone. Make call reviews a weekly non-negotiable, not an occasional exercise. How to Use Your Professional Network to Sharpen Your Cold Calling Game Your professional network is one of the most underutilized resources for improving cold calling skills. Connecting with fellow sales professionals — through LinkedIn communities, sales-focused Slack groups, or industry events — exposes you to diverse tactics, scripts, and objection-handling frameworks you'd never encounter in isolation. Peer learning is particularly powerful because it comes from practitioners who face the same real-world challenges you do. Sharing call recordings, swapping scripts, and discussing what's working in your specific market creates a collaborative intelligence loop. The best reps are never learning in a vacuum; they are constantly benchmarking against and learning from their peers. Why Staying Current on Industry Trends Makes You a Better Cold Caller Cold calling doesn't happen in a vacuum — it happens inside a specific industry context. When you understand the macro trends, regulatory changes, and competitive pressures affecting your prospect's world, your calls immediately become more relevant and credible. A rep who references a recent industry development earns instant authority; a rep who sounds out of touch loses credibility before the pitch even begins. Dedicate time each week to reading industry publications, following relevant thought leaders, and monitoring your target accounts' news. This intelligence becomes the raw material for highly personalized, timely outreach that resonates far beyond a generic cold call. The reps who consistently outperform their peers are not necessarily the most naturally gifted; they are the ones who invest in both the soft skills that build human connection and the hard skills that drive measurable outcomes. From building instant relatability to navigating gatekeepers with confidence, every skill covered in this article represents a lever you can pull to improve your close rate.
